AvifKit is stable. The public API is what it will stay — additions from here, no removals or
signature changes without a 2.0.0. Nothing in this release removes or renames anything that
existed in 0.3.2; upgrading is a version-string change.

Two features land with it, and both change what existing code produces.

## Animated GIFs become animated AVIF

A GIF used to convert to a still — first frame, animation gone. It now becomes an AVIF image
sequence: every frame, its own delay, the same loop count. The decoder is pure Kotlin in
`commonMain`, so Android and iOS produce the same frames from the same file, and frames stream
one at a time rather than batching — a 48-frame 800x600 animation peaks at one frame either side
of the JNI boundary instead of 92 MB.

**What changes for you:** if you convert GIFs and want the old still-image behaviour, set
`EncodingOptions(encodeAnimation = false)`. Everything else is new surface with defaults:
`ImageInfo.frameCount` / `durationMillis` / `loopCount` / `isAnimated`, and `decodeAvifFrames`.

## EXIF and XMP survive the conversion

`preserveMetadata` has been a documented no-op since the option existed — capture date, camera,
lens, GPS and edit history were stripped on the way to AVIF. It works now. The raw EXIF and XMP
payloads are copied via `avifImageSetMetadataExif`/`avifImageSetMetadataXMP`, parsed in
`commonMain` rather than through `ExifInterface`/`ImageIO`, because neither platform exposes the
blob libavif wants — only parsed attributes, which quietly drop maker notes and anything else the
platform doesn't model.

JPEG, PNG and WebP sources are read. HEIC keeps its metadata in ISOBMFF items this library does
not parse, and a GIF has nowhere to put EXIF, so animated output carries none.

**What changes for you:** if you were relying on `preserveMetadata = true` doing nothing, it no
longer does nothing — converted images now carry their source tags, GPS included. Set it to
`false` to strip.

An iOS orientation bug the metadata tests uncovered is fixed in the same release.

## Codecs

libavif 1.4.2 and AOM 3.14.1, replacing a patch that had silently stopped applying — every CMake
configure was cloning libaom from googlesource rather than using the vendored offline source.
